messages:
tala: Quick heads-up: I hit inconsistent auth precedence between the JS SDK (v0.9.1) and the Go CLI. Local dev flow: REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env, REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID pointing to corp project. Edge lambda uses env, CLI uses metadata -> ends up with cross-tenant auth errors.

ben: can you paste the minimal repro? curious if it's env loading order or if project-scoped tokens are being applied server-side incorrectly.

tala: repro: 1) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_user_test  2) export REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID=proj-corp  3) run `rw dev` (go cli) and hit /api/chat -> 401 intermittently. In local Chrome it sometimes works, Postman fails.

oliver: sounds like two problems: (A) env provider order mismatch across SDKs, (B) server treats presence of REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID as an override and tries to resolve service keys for that project. we should not implicitly re-scope a user key to another project.

maya: agreed. UX wise we need: (1) documented precedence (ENV > session-file > file > metadata) in a central place, (2) warning when REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID look like they belong to different orgs, (3) an explicit opt-in for cross-tenant scoping.

ben: implementation note: adding a startup validate call (/v1/auth/validate) is cheap but noisy for CI. we can gate it behind REDWOOD_ENV_STRICT=true so only strict devs opt in.

oliver: runtime concern: when keys rotate, the short window where some processes have refreshed credentials and others still have old mapping is causing 401 spikes. suggestion: credential-refresh should broadcast versioned tokens and fallback to previous token for 30s while retries happen.

tala: could we instead add a simple header check: if request contains X-Redwood-Project mismatch with token owner, return 4xx with a clear message instead of generic 401? saves time debugging.

maya: yes, but that requires server-side change. file an API bug for clearer error codes + message. I'll draft one.

sdk-bot: Note: please add an SDK integration test that covers the four env permutations (only API_KEY, API_KEY + PROJECT, project-only metadata, session-file priority). See CONTRIBUTING.md for test harness.

ben: action plan: 1) oliver to add env-provider parity patch in Go & JS (ensure same order) + unit tests; 2) maya to open API bug for better error message on project/token mismatch; 3) tala to add sampleapp startup warning when REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID present; 4) ben to prototype token-broadcast refresh/backoff.

oliver: will open PR for provider parity today and include a small compat note in changelog.

maya: i'll author the API bug and link to the parity PR when ready.

tala: thanks all. this explains several support tickets I triaged this week. also adding a quick troubleshooting blurb in sampleapp README: "If you see intermittent 401s locally, check that your REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID belong to the same org."

ben: perfect. leaving this thread here. tagging @sdk-team for visibility :eyes:
